title: Chapter 4.  Merger with India & the Path to Statehood

blocks.content: Manipur's transition from independent princely state to Indian state followed an unusually distinct sequence — a brief period as a constitutional monarchy with its own elected legislature, followed by a merger agreement that remains, to this day, a subject of continued political debate within Manipur. This background is essential for understanding Chapter 12's coverage of contemporary identity politics.

Following India's independence in August 1947, Manipur — still nominally a princely state under Maharaja Bodhchandra Singh — adopted its own written constitution, the Manipur State Constitution Act, 1947, establishing a constitutional monarchy with an elected Manipur State Legislative Assembly, making Manipur one of the very few princely states in India to hold its own democratic elections and establish a functioning elected legislature BEFORE fully merging with India.

Elections to this Manipur State Legislative Assembly were held in 1948, and the resulting Assembly functioned for a brief period, representing a distinctive and often-cited chapter in Manipur's political history as a democratically self-governing entity in its own right, prior to the merger process described below.

★ EXAM POINT: Manipur held its OWN state elections and had its own functioning elected legislature in 1948 — BEFORE its full merger with India — a distinctive fact frequently cited in discussions of Manipur's historical political identity and referenced in contemporary debates about the state's relationship with the Indian Union.

In September 1949, Maharaja Bodhchandra Singh signed the Manipur Merger Agreement with the Governor-General of India (V.P. Menon representing the Government of India), under which Manipur's administration merged fully into the Indian Union, and the existing Manipur State Legislative Assembly (elected in 1948) was dissolved.

The circumstances and process surrounding this 1949 merger — including questions about the degree of the Maharaja's free consent versus political pressure, and the absence of ratification by the elected 1948 State Assembly before its dissolution — have remained a matter of continued historical and political controversy within Manipur, cited by various political and civil-society voices at different points as evidence of an incomplete or contested process of accession, a sensitive and still-debated historical question that candidates should treat as a genuine subject of ongoing discussion rather than a fully settled matter.

Following the merger, Manipur was administered initially as a Part C State (a category of centrally administered territories under the original Constitution, similar to Delhi's early post-Independence status, covered in the companion Delhi GS volume), and subsequently reorganised as a Union Territory under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

★ EXAM POINT: The 1949 Manipur Merger Agreement's contested circumstances remain a genuinely debated historical topic within Manipur — candidates should present this as an area of continued discussion (citing the facts: what was signed, when, and the absence of prior Assembly ratification) rather than asserting a single definitive interpretation of its legitimacy.

Manipur was administered as a Union Territory from 1956 (following the States Reorganisation Act) for the next roughly sixteen years, a period during which sustained regional political demands for full statehood — driven by concerns over inadequate representation and developmental neglect under centrally administered UT status — gradually built momentum.

Manipur was granted full statehood on 21 January 1972, together with Meghalaya and Tripura, under the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971 — a landmark piece of legislation that reorganised the administrative map of India's North-East, also creating Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram as Union Territories at the same time (both attaining full statehood later, in 1987).

cells: Manipur State Constitution Act adopted; state constitutional monarchy established
Manipur Merger Agreement signed; Assembly dissolved; merger with India
Manipur becomes a Union Territory (States Reorganisation Act, 1956)
Manipur attains full statehood (North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971), together with Meghalaya and Tripura

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: 21 January 1972 is Manipur's Statehood Day — celebrated together with Meghalaya and Tripura (all three attained statehood on the same date, under the same 1971 Act) — a frequently tested shared-date fact distinguishing Statehood Day from the earlier Patriots' Day (13 August, Chapter 3).

items: Manipur State Constitution Act (1947) established a constitutional monarchy with an elected State Legislative Assembly (elections held 1948) — before full merger with India.
Manipur Merger Agreement signed September 1949 (Maharaja Bodhchandra Singh & V.P. Menon); the Agreement's contested circumstances remain a debated historical topic within Manipur.
Manipur was a Union Territory from 1956 (States Reorganisation Act) until attaining full statehood.
Full statehood: 21 January 1972, together with Meghalaya and Tripura, under the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971.
